paragraphs.text: Pontotoc’s share of the sales tax Mississippi collected in October was $336,838.80, up from $299,216.91 a year earlier. The $37,621.89 gain amounts to 12.6%, according to the Mississippi Department of Revenue’s latest municipal report.

October accounted for nearly all of the city’s gain since July 1. At the end of September, Pontotoc was only $352.66 ahead of the same three months last year. With October included, its four-month total reached $1,367,981.51, up $37,974.55, or 2.9%.

Sherman’s October share rose to $70,673.01, a 12.4% gain from a year earlier. Ecru’s rose 9.7% to $27,737.34. Thaxton was nearly even, with $4,402.11 this October and $4,397.78 last October. Algoma moved in the other direction, falling from $6,126.86 to $4,868.80, a drop of 20.5%.

The month on the report matters. Retailers collect tax from customers, send it to the state the following month, and the state pays the municipal share a month later. October labels the middle step. On that timetable, the report reflects September shopping and a November payment to the cities.
